problem: NaVid, a video-based VLN-CE model, accumulates historical visual tokens and KV cache with each step, so GPU memory and inference latency grow during navigation and hinder deployment.
motivation: Efficient deployment of video-based embodied navigation models on robots needs bounded memory and latency. Historical visual tokens dominate the growth, so sparsifying them could cut cost without destroying navigation quality.
key_idea: Sparsify NaVid's historical visual tokens and KV cache using three strategies (Uniform, FastV-NaVid, GroupAttn) and compare their trade-offs.
insight: Per the abstract, the strategies trade off differently. Uniform gives the most direct memory compression, FastV-NaVid works better at medium-to-high keep ratios, and GroupAttn best preserves frame-level semantic integrity and trajectory similarity (nDTW). No single method dominates on SR, SPL, nDTW, memory and time. Only the abstract was available, so the detailed ablations are not visible.
method: Uniform: sparsifies historical visual tokens by uniform sampling to a target keep ratio, giving direct memory compression.
FastV-NaVid: adapts FastV-style attention-based token pruning to NaVid's historical visual tokens/KV cache.
GroupAttn: groups tokens (frame-level) and uses attention to select them, preserving frame-level semantic integrity.
Evaluation: compares the methods on SR, SPL, nDTW, memory reduction and latency at various keep ratios on VLN-CE.

setting.backbone: NaVid (video-based VLM, pretrained; sparsification applied at inference)
setting.training_data: none stated for the sparsification (inference-time modification of NaVid)

results: The abstract reports that historical visual sparsification reduces dynamic memory pressure and improves latency-related indicators in part of the navigation process. Uniform gives the clearest memory reduction, FastV-NaVid does better at medium-to-high keep ratios, and GroupAttn best preserves nDTW and semantics. No numbers are given.
limitations: Latency gains occur only in part of the navigation process
Trade-offs among SR, SPL, nDTW and memory with no single best method
Evaluated on a single model (NaVid) and in simulation, as far as the abstract shows
